usage.rejection: After reject or dismiss, out of hand means immediately and without serious consideration.
usage.control: After be or get, it can mean beyond control: The situation is out of hand.
usage.word_order: In the rejection sense, the phrase usually follows the object: reject the proposal out of hand.
usage.evaluation: Rejecting something out of hand often suggests that the decision was hasty, categorical, or insufficiently considered.
usage.distinction: Get out of hand describes the process of becoming uncontrolled, whereas be out of hand describes the resulting state.
usage.spelling: The idiom is written as three separate words and is not the same as hand out, meaning distribute.

ja: 提案・主張・可能性などを十分に検討せず即座に退けて
議論や要求を初めから受け入れる余地なく拒絶して
証拠や詳細を調べる前に、問題外として扱って
be out of hand の形で、状況・行動などが制御不能で
get out of hand の形で、事態が手に負えない状態になって
en: by rejecting a proposal, argument, or possibility immediately without serious consideration
by refusing to entertain a request or claim from the outset
by treating something as unacceptable before examining its evidence or details
in be out of hand, beyond effective control
in get out of hand, becoming uncontrollable or unmanageable

nuance.ja: reject something out of hand は、単に最終的に拒絶するのではなく、内容を本格的に検討する前に「問題外だ」と即座に退けることを表す。その判断が断固としていることを示す場合もあるが、文脈によっては早計・不公正・閉鎖的だという批判を含む。The court rejected the argument out of hand なら、裁判所がその主張を容易に、またはほとんど検討に値しないものとして退けたという強い表現になる。一方、The situation is out of hand は「事態が制御不能である」という別の意味である。既存の get out of hand は制御可能な状態から制御不能へ移る変化を表し、be out of hand はその状態自体を表す。
nuance.en: To reject something out of hand is not merely to reject it after deliberation. It means refusing it immediately or treating it as unworthy of serious consideration from the outset. The phrase can emphasize decisiveness, but it may also criticize a decision as hasty, unfair, or closed-minded. The court rejected the argument out of hand strongly suggests that the argument was disposed of readily or regarded as scarcely deserving consideration. By contrast, The situation is out of hand uses a separate sense meaning beyond control. Get out of hand describes the transition from a manageable condition to an uncontrolled one, while be out of hand describes the resulting state.

ja: out of hand：検討せず即座に退けて。または制御不能な状態で。
get out of hand：状況・行動などが手に負えなくなる。
reject：提案・主張・申請などを受け入れないと決定する。
dismiss：主張・懸念などを重要でない、または根拠がないとして退ける。
rule out：選択肢・可能性を検討対象から除外する。
summarily：通常の手続きや十分な検討を経ず、即座に。
offhand：事前の準備や十分な検討をせず、その場で。
out of control：人・状況・機械などが制御できない状態で。
en: out of hand means immediately and without serious consideration, or in another sense beyond control.
get out of hand means becoming too difficult or disorderly to control.
reject means deciding not to accept a proposal, argument, application, or other submission.
dismiss means treating a claim, concern, or idea as unimportant or unsupported.
rule out means excluding an option or possibility from further consideration.
summarily means immediately and without following the usual procedure or giving full consideration.
offhand means without preparation or sufficient prior thought.
out of control describes a person, situation, or machine that can no longer be effectively managed.

etymology.ja: out of hand には、歴史的に複数の意味が発達した。hand は人が物を保持・操作する身体部位であることから、in hand は「支配下にある」、out of hand は「手の届く支配から外れた」、すなわち「制御不能な」という意味を持つようになった。一方、拒絶に関する out of hand は「直ちに、その場で」という古い副詞的用法から発達し、reject out of hand が「時間をかけて検討せず即座に退ける」という意味になった。したがって、制御不能と即時拒絶の意味は、現代では同じ綴りを持つものの、文中の動詞によって区別される。
etymology.en: Out of hand has developed several historically related but distinct uses. Because the hand is the means by which a person holds and controls an object, in hand came to suggest control, while out of hand could describe something beyond one’s grasp or control. A separate adverbial use of out of hand meant immediately or without delay. In constructions such as reject out of hand, this developed into the meaning of refusing something at once without prolonged or serious consideration. The modern senses of uncontrolled and summarily rejected are normally distinguished by the accompanying verb and context.

note.ja: 通常の手続き・説明・十分な検討を省き、即座に処理することを表す形式的な語。
note.en: A formal adverb describing action taken immediately without the usual procedure, explanation, or full consideration.

note.ja: 提案・主張・事情などを検討に入れずに判断することを明示する。
note.en: Explicitly states that a proposal, argument, or circumstance was not taken into account before a decision.

note.ja: 個別事情を検討せず、規則・反応などに従って当然のように処理する。
note.en: Describes a result occurring as a matter of rule or immediate response without individualized deliberation.

note.ja: 状況・行動・機械などが管理・抑制できない状態にある。
note.en: Describes a situation, behavior, or machine that cannot be effectively managed or restrained.

note.ja: 問題・量・人物などが大きすぎたり複雑すぎたりして、処理・管理できない。
note.en: Describes a problem, quantity, or person too difficult or complex to handle effectively.

equivalents.es: rechazar de plano / fuera de control

ja: reject a proposal out of hand — 提案を検討せず即座に拒絶する
dismiss an idea out of hand — 考えを頭ごなしに退ける
reject an argument out of hand — 主張を一蹴する
dismiss a complaint out of hand — 苦情をまともに検討せず退ける
rule out a possibility out of hand — 可能性を初めから排除する
not reject something out of hand — 何かを初めから拒絶しない
be rejected out of hand — 即座に拒絶される
an application dismissed out of hand — 簡単に退けられた申請
the situation is out of hand — 事態は制御不能である
the crowd is getting out of hand — 群衆が手に負えなくなっている
before matters get out of hand — 事態が制御不能になる前に
prevent the dispute from getting out of hand — 紛争が手に負えなくなるのを防ぐ
en: reject a proposal out of hand
dismiss an idea out of hand
reject an argument out of hand
dismiss a complaint out of hand
rule out a possibility out of hand
not reject something out of hand
be rejected out of hand
an application dismissed out of hand
the situation is out of hand
the crowd is getting out of hand
before matters get out of hand
prevent the dispute from getting out of hand

ja: We should not reject her proposal out of hand without examining the details. — 詳細を検討せず、彼女の提案を初めから退けるべきではありません。
The manager dismissed the complaint out of hand instead of speaking to the employees involved. — 管理職は関係する従業員から話を聞かず、その苦情を一蹴した。
Although the idea sounds unusual, I would not rule it out of hand. — その考えは珍しく聞こえるが、私は初めから可能性を排除するつもりはない。
By the time the police arrived, the situation was completely out of hand. — 警察が到着したときには、事態は完全に制御不能になっていた。
A patent examiner should not reject an argument out of hand merely because the applicant relies on an unconventional interpretation. — 出願人が通常とは異なる解釈に依拠しているというだけで、特許審査官はその主張を検討せずに退けるべきではない。
en: We should not reject her proposal out of hand without examining the details.
The manager dismissed the complaint out of hand instead of speaking to the employees involved.
Although the idea sounds unusual, I would not rule it out of hand.
By the time the police arrived, the situation was completely out of hand.
A patent examiner should not reject an argument out of hand merely because the applicant relies on an unconventional interpretation.

forms.third_person_singular: get his / her / its act together

grammar.transitivity: fixed idiomatic construction with a possessive determiner
patterns: need to get one’s act together
try to get one’s act together
help someone get their act together
tell someone to get their act together
get one’s act together before + clause
get one’s act together and + verb
If we don’t get our act together, + clause
It’s time to get your act together.

usage.possessive: The possessive determiner agrees with the person being discussed: get my, your, his, her, our, or their act together.
usage.meaning: The idiom means becoming organized, disciplined, prepared, or effective after a period of confusion or poor performance.
usage.direct_command: Get your act together can sound critical, impatient, or insulting when used as a direct command.
usage.self_reference: I need to get my act together is a common self-critical acknowledgment that improvement or organization is necessary.
usage.not_literal: Act does not normally refer to a theatrical performance in current idiomatic use.
usage.register: It is informal; become properly organized, improve performance, or take corrective action is more suitable in formal writing.

ja: 混乱している仕事・生活・考え方などを整理する
無責任・非効率な行動を改め、きちんと行動する
必要な準備を整え、効果的に仕事ができる状態になる
問題を放置せず、自制心を持って立て直す
個人・組織が不調や失敗から脱し、適切に機能し始める
en: to organize one’s confused work, life, or thinking
to correct irresponsible or ineffective behavior and begin acting properly
to make the preparations necessary to perform effectively
to stop neglecting problems and restore discipline or control
for a person or organization, to recover from disorder or poor performance and function properly

nuance.ja: get one’s act together は、能力が全くないというより、能力を発揮するための整理・準備・集中・自制が不足している状態から立ち直ることを表す。I need to get my act together なら、自分の遅れや混乱を認めて「しっかりしなければ」と述べる自然な自己批判になる。一方、Get your act together! と他人に命令すると、「いい加減しっかりしろ」「ちゃんとやれ」という強い非難になり得る。個人だけでなく、Our department needs to get its act together のように組織にも使える。単に部屋や書類を物理的に片づけるだけではなく、行動・計画・仕事ぶり全体を立て直す意味を持つ。
nuance.en: Get one’s act together usually suggests not a complete lack of ability but a failure to organize, prepare, concentrate, or exercise the discipline needed to use that ability effectively. I need to get my act together is a natural self-critical admission that the speaker must become more responsible or organized. Directed at another person, Get your act together! can be a forceful rebuke meaning that the person must stop behaving incompetently or irresponsibly. The idiom can also describe an organization, as in Our department needs to get its act together. It concerns overall conduct, planning, or performance rather than merely arranging physical objects.

ja: get one’s act together：混乱や不調を立て直し、責任を持って効率的に行動する。
pull oneself together：動揺・悲しみ・恐怖などを抑え、平静と自制を取り戻す。
get organized：物・予定・仕事などを整理し、計画的に行動できる状態になる。
shape up：態度・仕事ぶり・体調などを改善する。命令では強い批判になり得る。
sort oneself out：個人的な問題・混乱を整理し、適切に対処する。特にイギリス英語。
get a grip：感情・行動を制御し、現実的に考える。直接言うと批判的。
straighten oneself out：生活・考え・問題を整理し、安定した状態へ戻す。
take corrective action：問題を改善するため、具体的な是正措置を取る形式的な表現。
en: get one’s act together means overcoming disorder or poor performance and beginning to act responsibly and effectively.
pull oneself together means recovering emotional calm and self-control after distress or shock.
get organized means arranging one’s possessions, schedule, or work so that one can act systematically.
shape up means improving one’s behavior, performance, or physical condition and can sound strongly critical as a command.
sort oneself out means resolving personal problems or confusion and is especially common in British English.
get a grip means controlling one’s emotions or behavior and thinking realistically, often with a critical tone.
straighten oneself out means resolving disorder in one’s life, thinking, or behavior and returning to stability.
take corrective action is a formal expression for adopting specific measures to remedy a problem.

etymology.ja: この表現の act は、演劇の「演技・出し物」から、人が他人に見せる行動・仕事ぶり・一連の活動という意味へ広がった。together は、ばらばらの要素を一つのまとまりある状態にすることを示す。get one’s act together は、必要な要素をまとめ、まともな演技や仕事を行える状態に整えるという比喩から、「行動・生活・仕事を立て直す」という意味になったと考えられる。現代では演劇との結び付きは通常意識されず、個人や組織が混乱・準備不足・非効率を克服することを表す一般的な口語表現である。
etymology.en: Act developed from its theatrical meaning of a performance or part of a performance into broader senses involving a person’s conduct, presentation, or organized activity. Together conveys bringing separate or disordered elements into a coherent whole. Get one’s act together consequently evokes assembling everything required to perform properly and developed the figurative meaning of organizing one’s conduct, life, or work. In present-day use, speakers do not normally intend a direct theatrical reference; the idiom broadly describes overcoming confusion, inadequate preparation, or ineffective performance.

note.ja: 予定・情報・仕事・持ち物などを整理し、効率的に行動できる状態になる。
note.en: To arrange one’s schedule, information, work, or possessions so that effective action becomes possible.

note.ja: 不十分な態度・成績・仕事ぶりなどを改善する。相手に使うと厳しい。
note.en: To improve inadequate conduct or performance, often sounding severe when directed at another person.

note.ja: 感情的な動揺を抑え、冷静さや自制心を取り戻す。
note.en: To regain emotional calm and self-control after becoming distressed or overwhelmed.

note.ja: 自分の生活・感情・問題を整理して、より安定した状態にする。
note.en: To resolve disorder in one’s life, emotions, or personal problems and become more stable.

note.ja: 態度や行動を改めて、規律正しく適切に振る舞う。
note.en: To correct one’s conduct and begin behaving in a more disciplined or appropriate manner.

get your act together — しっかりする、行動を改める

get your act together
get our act together

ja: I need to get my act together and finish all these unfinished tasks. — しっかり態勢を立て直して、未完了の仕事をすべて終わらせなければなりません。
If we don’t get our act together soon, we’ll miss the deadline. — 私たちが早く態勢を整えなければ、締切に間に合わなくなります。
She finally got her act together and began managing her finances carefully. — 彼女はようやく生活を立て直し、家計を慎重に管理し始めた。
Telling an exhausted employee to get their act together may make the situation worse. — 疲れ切った従業員にしっかりしろと言うと、状況を悪化させる場合がある。
The applicant must get its act together before filing and ensure that the claims, drawings, and specification are mutually consistent. — 出願人は出願前に態勢を整え、請求項・図面・明細書が相互に整合していることを確認しなければならない。
en: I need to get my act together and finish all these unfinished tasks.
If we don’t get our act together soon, we’ll miss the deadline.
She finally got her act together and began managing her finances carefully.
Telling an exhausted employee to get their act together may make the situation worse.
The applicant must get its act together before filing and ensure that the claims, drawings, and specification are mutually consistent.

grammar.transitivity: intransitive idiomatic construction, commonly followed by a that-clause
patterns: It goes without saying that + clause
It almost goes without saying that + clause
It should go without saying that + clause
It hardly needs saying that + clause
This should go without saying, but + clause
although it goes without saying that + clause
leave something unsaid because it goes without saying

usage.dummy_it: The standard construction uses anticipatory it followed by a that-clause: It goes without saying that safety comes first.
usage.that_omission: That may be omitted in informal usage, although retaining it usually makes a long sentence clearer.
usage.response: That goes without saying can stand alone as a response meaning that the point is obvious or already accepted.
usage.tense: The present form goes is by far the most common; went without saying is possible when describing what was assumed in a past situation.
usage.tone: The expression can emphasize shared understanding, but it may sound condescending if the point is not actually obvious to the listener.
usage.distinction: It goes without saying is an idiom meaning something is obvious; go without food or go without sleeping means manage without something.

ja: あまりに明白なので、わざわざ言う必要がない
関係者の間ですでに当然の前提として理解されている
当然そうすべき、またはそうであると強調する
明示されていなくても、文脈上当然に認められる
That goes without saying. の形で「もちろんです」と同意する
en: to be so obvious that it does not need to be stated
to be already understood as a natural assumption among the people concerned
to emphasize that something unquestionably is or ought to be the case
to be accepted from the context even though it has not been expressly stated
in That goes without saying, to express agreement that something is obvious

nuance.ja: It goes without saying that ... は、内容を「言う必要がないほど当然だ」と位置づけながら、実際にはあえて言葉にして強調する修辞的な表現である。It goes without saying that we’ll help you なら、支援する意思を当然の前提として強く示す。好意・責任・安全などについて使えば安心感を与えられるが、議論のある問題について使うと、異論を最初から排除する高圧的な表現になり得る。また、法的文書では、当事者が当然だと考える事項でも明記が必要な場合が多いので、goes without saying を契約上の権利・義務の根拠として依存するべきではない。
nuance.en: It goes without saying that is rhetorically interesting because the speaker explicitly states something while presenting it as too obvious to require statement. It goes without saying that we’ll help you strongly frames the offer of assistance as a natural and unquestioned commitment. Used for goodwill, responsibility, or safety, it can provide reassurance. Used for a disputed proposition, however, it may sound condescending or may attempt to exclude disagreement without argument. In legal documents, matters that seem obvious may still require express wording, so goes without saying should not ordinarily be relied upon as the basis of a contractual right or obligation.

ja: go without saying：明白で、わざわざ言う必要がない。
needless to say：言うまでもなく。話者が当然と考える内容を付け加える。
of course：当然、もちろん。文脈により温かくも高圧的にも響く。
obviously：誰にでも明らかだと話者が考えることを直接示す。
self-evident：外部の証明を必要とせず、それ自体で明白な。
be understood：明言されなくても、共通の前提として理解されている。
be taken for granted：当然のものとして扱われ、十分に意識・評価されていない場合がある。
go without：必要な物・行為なしで生活・継続する。go without saying とは別構文。
en: go without saying means being so obvious that no express statement should be necessary.
needless to say introduces a point that the speaker regards as obvious or predictable.
of course marks something as natural or expected and can sound either reassuring or condescending.
obviously directly states that the speaker regards something as readily apparent.
self-evident describes something whose truth appears clear without external proof.
be understood means being accepted as a shared assumption even though it is not expressly stated.
be taken for granted means being treated as certain or natural, sometimes without adequate appreciation.
go without means managing without a necessary or desirable thing and is structurally distinct from go without saying.

etymology.ja: この表現の go は、物理的な移動ではなく、物事が特定の状態で通用・進行するという意味で使われている。without saying は「口に出されることなしに」を表すため、全体として「言葉にされなくてもそのまま通用する」、すなわち「明白なので言う必要がない」という意味になる。フランス語 cela va sans dire「それは言わずとも通る、言うまでもない」と非常によく対応し、英語表現の定着にはフランス語の影響があったとされる。現在では It goes without saying that ... が最も一般的な定型である。
etymology.en: In this expression, go does not describe physical movement but something passing, proceeding, or being accepted in a particular state. Without saying means without being expressed in words. The complete phrase therefore conveys that a proposition can pass unspoken because its truth or necessity is already apparent. It closely corresponds to French cela va sans dire, literally it goes without saying, and the French expression is generally associated with the establishment of the English idiom. It goes without saying that is now its most common fixed construction.

note.ja: 話者が予想可能・当然と考える内容を、「言うまでもないが」と導入する。
note.en: Introduces a statement that the speaker regards as natural, obvious, or readily predictable.

note.ja: 内容が当然・自然・予想どおりであることを表す一般的な表現。
note.en: A common expression indicating that something is natural, expected, or already accepted.

note.ja: 話者の判断では、事実・結論が容易に理解できるほど明白であることを示す。
note.en: Indicates that the speaker considers a fact or conclusion readily apparent.

note.ja: ある事項が明示されていなくても、関係者間の共通認識であることを示す。
note.en: States that a matter is accepted as a shared understanding even without explicit expression.

note.ja: 命題の真実性が外部の説明・証明を要しないほど明らかだと述べる形式的表現。
note.en: A formal expression asserting that a proposition is clear without external explanation or proof.

although it goes without saying that ... — ～は言うまでもないものの
something that goes without saying — わざわざ言う必要のないこと
a principle that should go without saying — 当然の前提であるべき原則
leave something unsaid because it goes without saying — 自明なので何かを明言しない
nothing goes without saying — 何事も言わなくてよいとは限らない
en: It goes without saying that ...
That goes without saying
It almost goes without saying
It should go without saying
It goes without saying that safety comes first
It goes without saying that we support you
This should go without saying, but ...
although it goes without saying that ...
something that goes without saying
a principle that should go without saying

ja: It goes without saying that the safety of the passengers comes first. — 乗客の安全が最優先であることは言うまでもない。
It should go without saying that employees must treat customers with respect. — 従業員が顧客に敬意を持って接しなければならないのは、本来言うまでもない。

usage.places: When applied to a place or atmosphere, it means quiet, peaceful, and free from interruption or conflict.

usage.comparison: More tranquil and most tranquil are normally preferred to tranquiller and tranquillest.
usage.spelling: The noun is commonly spelled tranquility in American English and tranquillity in British English.
usage.register: Tranquil is somewhat more descriptive, literary, or formal than the everyday adjective calm.

for a place or environment, quiet and peaceful

for a sea, lake, or surface of water, still or gently moving rather than rough

nuance.ja: tranquil は、単に音が小さいだけでなく、人の心を乱す刺激・不安・争いなどがなく、安定した静けさが続いている状態を表す。a tranquil garden は静かなだけでなく、そこで心が休まりそうな穏やかな庭を連想させる。人について使えば、感情が激しく動揺しておらず、内面的に平静であることを示す。calm は日常的で広く、一時的に興奮していない状態にも使える。serene は、より深く揺るぎない平穏や、表情・景色の美しさを強調しやすい。peaceful は騒音だけでなく、争い・暴力がないことにも広く使われる。tranquil はこれらの中間に位置し、やや文語的で情景描写に適している。
nuance.en: Tranquil describes not merely an absence of loud sound but a stable quietness undisturbed by anxiety, conflict, or intrusive activity. A tranquil garden suggests a peaceful setting in which the mind can rest. Applied to a person, it indicates inner composure and freedom from strong emotional disturbance. Calm is more common in everyday English and can describe a temporary absence of agitation. Serene often suggests deeper, more secure peace and may emphasize the beauty of a face or landscape. Peaceful applies broadly to freedom from noise, conflict, or violence. Tranquil lies between these ideas and is especially suitable for somewhat literary or evocative description.

etymology.ja: tranquil はフランス語 tranquille を経て、ラテン語 tranquillus「静かな、穏やかな」に由来する。ラテン語でも海・天候・人の心・社会の状態などが乱れていないことを表した。英語では、外部の騒音や動きが少ないという意味だけでなく、精神的な不安・興奮・対立から解放された平穏を表す語として定着した。同じ語族には名詞 tranquility／tranquillity「静穏、平穏」と、動詞 tranquilize／tranquillize「落ち着かせる、鎮静させる」がある。
etymology.en: Tranquil entered English through French tranquille from Latin tranquillus, meaning quiet, calm, or undisturbed. In Latin, it could describe a calm sea, peaceful weather, an untroubled mind, or a stable social condition. English retained both the external sense of freedom from noise or violent movement and the internal sense of release from anxiety, excitement, or conflict. Related forms include the noun tranquility in American spelling or tranquillity in British spelling and the verb tranquilize or tranquillize, meaning to calm or sedate.

usage.adjective: As an adjective, calm describes a person free from agitation or a situation, sea, or weather condition without violent activity.
usage.verb: As a transitive verb, calm means making someone or something less agitated; as an intransitive verb, it means becoming less agitated.

en: as an adjective, free from nervousness, anger, excitement, or emotional disturbance
for weather, the sea, or a situation, peaceful and without violent activity
as a noun, a state of peace without agitation, noise, wind, or disorder
as a verb, to reduce the fear, excitement, or agitation of a person or animal
for a situation, weather condition, or emotion, to become quiet and stable
to preserve composure and self-control during a crisis or disagreement

nuance.ja: calm は、人の感情から海・天候・社会状況まで幅広く使える、日常的で中立的な語である。a calm person は一時的に落ち着いている場合にも、普段から冷静な性格の場合にも使える。stay calm は困難な状況で平静を失わないこと、calm someone down は動揺している人を落ち着かせることを表す。ただし Calm down! と直接命令すると、相手の感情を軽視しているように響き、かえって怒らせることがある。tranquil は calm より描写的・文語的で、長く保たれる心地よい静けさを感じさせやすい。quiet は主に音や活動の少なさに焦点を置き、必ずしも感情の平静を意味しない。
nuance.en: Calm is an everyday and neutral word applicable to emotions, personality, weather, the sea, and social situations. A calm person may be temporarily composed or characteristically unexcitable. Stay calm emphasizes preserving composure during difficulty, while calm someone down means reducing that person’s agitation. The direct command Calm down! can sound dismissive of another person’s feelings and may increase rather than reduce anger. Tranquil is more descriptive or literary and often suggests pleasant, sustained quietness. Quiet primarily concerns the absence of sound or activity and does not necessarily imply emotional composure.

etymology.ja: calm はフランス語 calme を経て英語に入り、イタリア語・スペイン語・ポルトガル語などの同系語と関係する。そのさらに古い起源は、真昼の暑さや無風状態に関係する後期ラテン語・ギリシャ語系の語に求められることが多い。もとは海上で風が止まり、水面が動かない状態を表し、そこから天候全般の穏やかさ、社会的な静けさ、さらに人の感情が乱れていない状態へ意味が広がった。現代の綴りにある l は発音されず、名詞・形容詞・動詞のすべてで同じ発音になる。
etymology.en: Calm entered English through French calme and is related to corresponding forms in Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese. Its deeper history is commonly associated with Late Latin and Greek words connected with the heat or stillness of midday. It originally described a period at sea when the wind ceased and the water became still. The meaning expanded from quiet weather and water to social peace and finally to freedom from emotional agitation. The l in the modern spelling is silent, and the noun, adjective, and verb have the same pronunciation.

usage.uncountable: Food for thought is normally uncountable: some food for thought, not a food for thought.
usage.meaning: The expression refers to information or an idea that deserves careful consideration rather than a question requiring an immediate answer.
usage.article: The phrase usually appears without an article, although the food for thought may be possible when referring to previously identified material.
usage.evaluation: It normally has a positive or neutral tone, suggesting that something is intellectually stimulating or worthy of reflection.
usage.response: That’s food for thought is a natural response meaning that a point deserves further consideration.
usage.register: The expression is natural in conversation, journalism, education, speeches, and moderately formal business writing.

ja: 注意深く考える価値のある情報・意見

en: information or an opinion worthy of careful consideration
material that can deepen a judgment or discussion
something that causes a person to reconsider a previous view
an issue to be reflected upon rather than answered immediately
an intellectual stimulus that produces new perspectives or questions

nuance.ja: food for thought は、食べ物が身体を養うように、情報・意見・経験が思考を養うという比喩である。単に interesting「興味深い」というだけでなく、聞いた後も考え続ける価値があることを示す。The report provides food for thought と言えば、その報告書が直ちに採用すべき結論を示したというより、今後の判断や議論に役立つ論点を提示したという意味になる。通常は好意的または中立的だが、不都合な事実や警告が深刻な再検討を促す場合にも使える。必ずしも具体的な解決策や証拠を意味するわけではない。
nuance.en: Food for thought is based on the metaphor that information, opinions, or experiences nourish the mind just as physical food nourishes the body. It means more than merely interesting: the subject deserves continued reflection after it has been encountered. The report provides food for thought suggests that the report offers useful issues for future judgment or discussion, rather than necessarily presenting a conclusion that should immediately be adopted. The expression is normally positive or neutral, but an uncomfortable fact or warning can also provide serious food for thought. It does not necessarily constitute evidence or a concrete solution.

etymology.ja: food for thought は、食物が身体に栄養を与えることを、考えや知識が精神に刺激・栄養を与えることになぞらえた比喩表現である。food は古英語 fōda「食物・栄養」に由来し、thought は think の過去分詞に関連する古英語の名詞から発達した。英語では food が古くから、物理的な食物だけでなく、精神・感情・想像力を養うものの比喩として使われてきた。そこから food for thought が、思考の対象となり、熟考を促す情報・着想を表す定型表現として定着した。
etymology.en: Food for thought uses nourishment as a metaphor: ideas and information stimulate or sustain the mind as food sustains the body. Food derives from Old English fōda, meaning nourishment or something eaten, while thought developed from an Old English noun related to the verb think. English has long used food figuratively for something that nourishes the mind, emotions, or imagination. Food for thought consequently became an established expression for information or an idea that supplies material for continued reflection.

patterns: the pros and cons of + noun

usage.plural: The fixed phrase is normally plural: the pros and cons of the proposal.
usage.individual_items: An individual advantage or disadvantage may informally be called a pro or a con.
usage.prepositions: Use of after the complete phrase: the pros and cons of working remotely. To is common in there are pros and cons to working remotely.
usage.gerund: After of or to, a verb normally takes the gerund: the pros and cons of relocating.
usage.evaluation: The phrase encourages a balanced comparison but does not necessarily imply that the advantages and disadvantages have equal weight.
usage.register: Pros and cons is natural in conversation and business communication; advantages and disadvantages may be preferable in highly formal writing.

ja: 計画・選択・行動などの長所と短所
決定によって生じる利点と不利な点
ある問題について賛成・反対の根拠となる要素
複数の選択肢を比較する際に検討すべき肯定的・否定的側面
判断を下す前に比較衡量する利益とリスク
en: the advantages and disadvantages of a plan, choice, or action
the favorable and unfavorable consequences of a decision
factors supporting and opposing a particular position
the positive and negative aspects considered when comparing alternatives
the benefits and risks weighed before reaching a judgment

nuance.ja: pros and cons は、単純な賛成派と反対派ではなく、対象そのものが持つ具体的な利点・欠点を列挙し、比較する表現である。We discussed the pros and cons of remote work なら、在宅勤務に賛成か反対かを述べるだけでなく、柔軟性・通勤時間・意思疎通・孤立などの各要因を検討したことを示す。weigh the pros and cons は、それぞれの項目を単に数えるのではなく、重要性や影響の大きさまで比較することを表す。pros and cons は比較的くだけているが、業務上の会議や説明資料でも自然に使える。法律意見書や正式な報告書では advantages and disadvantages、benefits and risks などの方が明確な場合がある。
nuance.en: Pros and cons refers not merely to groups of supporters and opponents but to the specific favorable and unfavorable features of the matter itself. We discussed the pros and cons of remote work suggests consideration of individual factors such as flexibility, commuting time, communication, and isolation. To weigh the pros and cons means comparing not only the number of points on each side but also their importance and likely impact. The phrase is conversational but remains natural in workplace meetings and presentations. In a formal legal opinion or report, advantages and disadvantages or benefits and risks may sometimes provide greater precision.

ja: pros and cons：計画・選択肢などの長所と短所、利点と不利な点。
advantages and disadvantages：長所と短所を表す中立的で形式的な表現。
benefits and drawbacks：得られる利益と、それに伴う欠点・不都合。
benefits and risks：期待される利益と、発生する可能性のある危険。
strengths and weaknesses：人・計画・制度などの強みと弱み。
for and against：ある提案・主張への賛成論と反対論。
trade-offs：一つの利点を得るため、別の利点を犠牲にする関係。
cost-benefit analysis：費用と期待される利益を体系的に比較する分析。
en: pros and cons are the advantages and disadvantages of a plan, choice, or action.
advantages and disadvantages is a neutral and relatively formal expression for positive and negative features.
benefits and drawbacks are the gains provided by something and the inconveniences or defects accompanying them.
benefits and risks are the expected favorable results and the possible dangers.
strengths and weaknesses are the effective and deficient aspects of a person, plan, or system.
for and against refers to arguments supporting and opposing a proposal or position.
trade-offs are situations in which obtaining one advantage requires sacrificing another.
a cost-benefit analysis systematically compares expected benefits with the costs required to obtain them.

etymology.ja: pros and cons はラテン語 pro et contra「賛成と反対」に由来する。pro は「～のために、～に賛成して」、contra は「～に反して、～に対して」を意味した。英語では当初 pro and con または arguments pro and con のように、議論の賛成側と反対側を表した。その後、pro と con がそれぞれ可算名詞として再解釈され、a pro、a con、複数形 pros and cons が成立した。現代では議論上の賛否だけでなく、計画・商品・選択肢などが持つ具体的な利点と欠点を広く表す。
etymology.en: Pros and cons derives from Latin pro et contra, meaning for and against. Pro meant for or in favor of, while contra meant against or in opposition to. English initially used expressions such as pro and con and arguments pro and con for the two sides of a debate. Pro and con were subsequently reanalyzed as countable nouns, producing a pro, a con, and the plural phrase pros and cons. Modern usage extends beyond arguments for and against a proposition to the practical advantages and disadvantages of plans, products, and choices.

note.ja: 肯定的側面と否定的側面を明確かつ中立的に表す、より形式的な表現。
note.en: A more formal expression clearly and neutrally identifying positive and negative features.

note.ja: ある選択から得られる利益と、それに伴って生じる欠点・不都合。
note.en: The favorable results obtained from a choice and the defects or inconveniences accompanying it.

note.ja: 人・組織・制度・提案などの優れた点と不十分な点。
note.en: The effective and deficient qualities of a person, organization, system, or proposal.

note.ja: 行動によって期待される利益と、将来発生する可能性のある損失・危険。
note.en: The favorable results expected from an action and the possible future dangers or losses.

note.ja: 特定の提案・立場を支持する理由と、それに反対する理由。
note.en: Reasons supporting a particular proposal or position and reasons opposing it.

The lower price is a major pro, but the lack of customer support is a serious con. — 価格の安さは大きな長所だが、顧客サポートがないことは重大な短所だ。

grammar.plural: big pictures, uncommon in the idiomatic sense
patterns: keep the big picture in mind
lose sight of the big picture

usage.article: The idiomatic noun phrase normally takes the definite article: see the big picture.
usage.meaning: It refers to the overall situation, including context, relationships, objectives, and long-term consequences.
usage.bigger_picture: The bigger picture is also common and emphasizes a broader perspective than the one currently being considered.
usage.adjective: Before a noun, big-picture is normally hyphenated: a big-picture approach.
usage.contrast: The expression frequently contrasts with details, individual incidents, or short-term concerns.
usage.register: It is common in conversation, management, strategy, and business writing but may be replaced by overall context or comprehensive perspective in highly formal prose.

ja: 個々の細部ではなく、状況・問題の全体像
出来事の背景・相互関係・長期的影響を含む大局
計画・組織・事業などの最終的な目的と全体的方向性
個別の情報がどのように結び付くかを示す包括的な見方
短期的な問題を越えて検討すべき、より広い文脈
en: the overall situation or problem rather than its individual details
a broad perspective including background, relationships, and long-term consequences
the ultimate purpose and general direction of a plan, organization, or business
a comprehensive view showing how individual pieces of information are connected
the wider context that should be considered beyond immediate or short-term concerns

nuance.ja: the big picture は、細部を無視することではなく、細部を全体の目的・背景・因果関係の中に位置づけることを表す。see the big picture は複数の要素がどのように関係しているかを理解する能力、focus on the big picture は細かな問題に過度に気を取られず、主要な目的や長期的結果を重視する姿勢を示す。一方、big-picture thinking だけを重視すると、実施に必要な細部を見落とす可能性もある。the bigger picture は、現在検討している範囲よりさらに広い社会的・歴史的・戦略的背景へ視野を広げる場合に使われる。
nuance.en: The big picture does not necessarily mean ignoring details. It means locating those details within the overall purpose, context, and network of causes and consequences. To see the big picture is to understand how multiple elements relate to one another. To focus on the big picture is to avoid becoming excessively distracted by minor problems and instead emphasize principal objectives and long-term results. An exclusive preference for big-picture thinking can nevertheless cause someone to overlook details necessary for implementation. The bigger picture commonly broadens the perspective beyond the scope currently under discussion to include wider social, historical, or strategic considerations.

ja: the big picture：細部ではなく、背景・目的・影響を含む状況全体。
the bigger picture：現在の視点よりもさらに広い文脈・全体像。
overview：主な要素を簡潔に示す全体的な説明・概観。
overall perspective：問題全体を一つのまとまりとして捉える包括的な視点。
broader context：個別の事実を取り巻く、より広い背景・事情。
bird’s-eye view：高い位置から見下ろすように全体を把握する見方。
big-picture thinking：細部よりも目的・戦略・長期的関係を重視する思考。
the details：全体を構成する個別の事実・手順・小さな要素。
en: the big picture is the overall situation, including its background, purpose, and consequences.
the bigger picture is a still broader context than the perspective currently being considered.
an overview is a concise general account presenting the principal elements of a subject.
an overall perspective is a comprehensive view of a problem as a unified whole.
the broader context consists of the wider circumstances surrounding an individual fact or event.
a bird’s-eye view is a perspective from which the whole can be observed as if from above.
big-picture thinking emphasizes purpose, strategy, and long-term relationships over individual details.
the details are the individual facts, procedures, or smaller elements constituting the whole.

etymology.ja: the big picture は、一枚の絵を近くから見れば個々の線や色しか見えないが、距離を取れば作品全体の構図と意味を把握できるという視覚的な比喩に基づく。picture はラテン語 pictura「絵、描くこと」に由来し、フランス語を経て英語に入った。そこから picture は、視覚的な絵だけでなく、状況について頭の中に形成される全体的な理解も表すようになった。big picture は20世紀に、細部と対比される状況全体・包括的視点を表す慣用句として広く定着した。
etymology.en: The big picture is based on a visual metaphor: viewed too closely, a picture may appear to consist only of individual lines and colors, whereas stepping back reveals its overall composition and meaning. Picture derives through French from Latin pictura, meaning a painting or the act of painting. The word consequently developed beyond a physical image to mean a mental representation or general understanding of a situation. During the twentieth century, big picture became widely established as an idiom for the overall situation or comprehensive perspective contrasted with individual details.

note.ja: 個々の要素を相互関係の中で捉え、問題全体を包括的に見る視点。
note.en: A comprehensive viewpoint that considers individual elements in relation to the whole.

note.ja: 個別の出来事・発言・判断を理解するために必要な、より広い背景事情。
note.en: The wider circumstances required to understand an individual event, statement, or decision.

note.ja: 主題の主要部分を細部に深入りせず簡潔に示す説明。
note.en: A general account presenting the principal features of a subject without extensive detail.

note.ja: 複雑な対象を高い位置から見下ろすように、全体として把握する見方。
note.en: A general view of a complex subject as though observing the whole from above.

note.ja: より大きな計画・状況全体の中で、個々の出来事を位置づける際に使う表現。
note.en: An expression used when placing individual events within a much larger plan or overall situation.

ja: Try to look at the big picture instead of worrying about every minor problem. — 小さな問題を一つ一つ心配するのではなく、全体像を見るようにしてください。
She understands the details but sometimes loses sight of the big picture. — 彼女は細部を理解しているが、ときどき大局を見失う。
The report helped us see the big picture and understand how the different problems were connected. — その報告書のおかげで、私たちは全体像を把握し、異なる問題がどのようにつながっているかを理解できた。
From a big-picture perspective, the temporary loss may be necessary for the company’s long-term growth. — 大局的な観点では、その一時的損失は会社の長期的成長に必要かもしれない。

A patent attorney must examine the wording of each claim carefully while keeping the client’s broader intellectual property strategy—the big picture—in mind. — 弁理士は各請求項の文言を慎重に検討すると同時に、顧客のより広範な知的財産戦略、すなわち全体像を念頭に置かなければならない。

usage.spelling: Artifact is the standard American spelling; artefact is common in British English, although artifact is also used.
usage.archaeology: In archaeology, an artifact is a movable object made, modified, or used by humans.
usage.science: In research, an artifact is an apparent result created by the experimental method, equipment, sampling, or data processing rather than by the phenomenon being studied.
usage.medicine: In medical imaging, an artifact is a misleading feature or distortion caused by movement, equipment, reconstruction, or another technical factor.
usage.software: In software development, an artifact is a file or package produced or used during development, building, testing, or deployment.
usage.figurative: Artifact of can describe something produced by a particular system, historical period, or method rather than an inherent feature of the subject.

ja: 人間によって作られ、加工され、または使用された物
考古学・歴史学上の遺物・人工物
特定の文化・時代・社会を示す物的資料
測定・実験・画像処理などによって人工的に生じた、本来存在しない結果・像
ソフトウェアの開発・ビルド・テストによって生成されるファイルや成果物
特定の制度・方法・歴史的事情によって生じた副産物
en: an object made, modified, or used by human beings
a human-made object studied in archaeology or history
a material object providing evidence of a particular culture, period, or society
an apparent result or feature artificially produced by measurement, experimentation, or image processing
a file or package generated during software development, building, testing, or deployment
a by-product produced by a particular system, method, or historical circumstance

nuance.ja: artifact の意味は分野によって評価が大きく異なる。考古学では、人間の活動を示す土器・道具・硬貨などの価値ある資料を指し、否定的な意味はない。科学・医学では、観察対象そのものではなく、測定装置・標本作製・被験者の動き・データ処理などによって生じた見かけ上の特徴を指し、誤った結論を避けるため除外・補正すべきものとなる。ITでは、実行ファイル・ライブラリー・ログ・テスト結果など、工程によって生成された成果物を中立的に表す。したがって an artifact of the method は「その方法が作り出した人工的結果」であり、歴史的遺物を意味しない。
nuance.en: The evaluation of artifact differs substantially by field. In archaeology, it is a valuable source of evidence about human activity, such as pottery, tools, or coins, and carries no negative implication. In science and medicine, it is an apparent feature produced by equipment, specimen preparation, participant movement, data processing, or another aspect of the method rather than by the subject itself. Such an artifact may need to be excluded or corrected to avoid a false conclusion. In computing, the word neutrally denotes an output such as an executable file, library, log, or test report. An artifact of the method therefore means an artificial result created by the method, not a historical object.

ja: artifact：人が作った物、または測定・処理によって人工的に生じた結果。
relic：過去の時代・人物から残された物で、歴史的・宗教的価値を持つことがある。
antiquity：古代の物品、または古代という時代。通常、非常に古い物を指す。
specimen：研究・検査・展示のために採取・選択された標本。
fossil：過去の生物の遺骸・痕跡が地層などに保存されたもの。
anomaly：通常のパターン・予測・基準から外れた異常な結果。
error：測定値・計算・判断などに含まれる誤りや偏差。
software artifact：開発・ビルド・テストなどの工程で生成・使用されるファイルや成果物。
en: an artifact is a human-made object or an artificial result produced by a method of observation or processing.
a relic is an object surviving from the past and may possess historical or religious importance.
an antiquity is an object from ancient times, or the term may refer to the ancient period itself.
a specimen is an example selected or collected for examination, research, or display.
a fossil is the preserved remains or trace of an organism from an earlier geological period.
an anomaly is a result that differs from an expected pattern, prediction, or standard.
an error is an inaccuracy or deviation in measurement, calculation, or judgment.
a software artifact is a file or deliverable generated or used during development, building, or testing.

etymology.ja: artifact はラテン語 arte factum「技術によって作られたもの」に由来する。arte は ars「技術、技能」の奪格形、factum は facere「作る」の過去分詞に由来し、全体として「人の技によって作られた物」という意味を持った。ここから、自然物と対比される人工物、とくに考古学上の遺物を表す意味が定着した。さらに科学では、自然に存在する現象ではなく、観察・実験の手続きによって作られた結果を指すようになった。アメリカ英語では artifact、イギリス英語では artefact の綴りが伝統的に多い。
etymology.en: Artifact derives from the Latin expression arte factum, meaning something made by skill. Arte is a form of ars, meaning art or skill, and factum derives from the past participle of facere, to make. The word consequently came to denote an object made by human workmanship rather than a naturally occurring object, especially in archaeology. Scientific usage extended the idea to a result created by the procedure of observation or experimentation rather than by the phenomenon under investigation. Artifact is standard in American English, while artefact has traditionally been common in British English.

note.ja: 過去の時代・文化・人物から残された物で、歴史的・宗教的な意義を持つことがある。
note.en: An object surviving from a past period, culture, or person and sometimes possessing historical or religious significance.

note.ja: 古代に由来する物品を表し、artifact より年代の古さを強調する。
note.en: An object originating in ancient times, emphasizing greater age than the general term artifact.

note.ja: 自然に形成された物ではなく、人間が作成・加工した物を直接的に表す。
note.en: A direct expression for an object created or modified by humans rather than formed naturally.

note.ja: 画像・音・信号・情報などが元の状態から不正確に変形したもの。
note.en: An inaccurate alteration of an image, sound, signal, or item of information from its original form.

note.ja: 主要な目的物を作る過程で、付随的・二次的に生じる物や結果。
note.en: A secondary object or result produced incidentally during a process directed toward another principal output.

ja: Archaeologists discovered several bronze artifacts near the ancient settlement. — 考古学者たちは古代集落の近くで、複数の青銅製遺物を発見した。
The museum preserves artifacts that illustrate the daily life of the region’s former inhabitants. — その博物館は、かつての地域住民の日常生活を示す遺物を保存している。
Researchers concluded that the unusual result was an artifact of the measurement process. — 研究者たちは、その異常な結果が測定過程によって人工的に生じたものだと結論づけた。
The deployment failed because the required build artifact was missing from the server. — 必要なビルド成果物がサーバーに存在しなかったため、デプロイに失敗した。

A prototype may constitute relevant evidence of the invention’s development, but whether it is prior art cannot be determined merely by calling it an artifact. — 試作品は発明の開発を示す関連証拠となり得るが、それを単に人工物と呼ぶだけでは、先行技術に該当するかどうかを判断できない。
en: Archaeologists discovered several bronze artifacts near the ancient settlement.
The museum preserves artifacts that illustrate the daily life of the region’s former inhabitants.
Researchers concluded that the unusual result was an artifact of the measurement process.
The deployment failed because the required build artifact was missing from the server.
A prototype may constitute relevant evidence of the invention’s development, but whether it is prior art cannot be determined merely by calling it an artifact.

patterns: proponents of the view that + clause
proponents argue / claim / maintain that + clause
become / remain a proponent of + noun

usage.preposition: Proponent is normally followed by of: a proponent of reform, not a proponent for reform.
usage.person: The noun usually refers to a person, organization, or group actively supporting and promoting an idea, proposal, theory, or policy.
usage.active_support: It often implies public, reasoned, or sustained advocacy rather than private agreement alone.
usage.clause: Use proponents of the view that when introducing a proposition supported by a group.
usage.opposite: Opponent is the ordinary contrasting term for someone who opposes the proposal or position.
usage.register: Proponent is common in academic, political, legal, scientific, and public-policy discussion and is more formal than supporter.

ja: 提案・政策・制度などを支持し、その採用を主張する人
理論・思想・見解などを積極的に擁護する人物
新しい方法・改革・技術などの導入を推進する人
議論において特定の立場を提示し、その正当性を主張する側
法律・計画などの成立・承認を求める個人・組織
en: a person who supports a proposal, policy, or system and argues for its adoption
someone who actively defends a theory, idea, or point of view
a person promoting the introduction of a new method, reform, or technology
the party presenting and defending a particular position in a debate
an individual or organization seeking the enactment or approval of a law or plan

nuance.ja: proponent は supporter より形式的で、単に賛成しているだけでなく、提案・理論・制度などを積極的に提示・擁護・推進する人を表すことが多い。a proponent of renewable energy なら、再生可能エネルギーに好意的なだけでなく、その利用拡大を公に主張する人物を連想させる。advocate と近いが、advocate は他人の権利・利益を代弁する意味にも広く使われる一方、proponent は特定の考え・計画・主張との結び付きが強い。提案を最初に考案した本人である必要はない。また、proponent という語自体は、支持される立場が正しいことを意味しない。
nuance.en: Proponent is more formal than supporter and often describes someone who actively presents, defends, or promotes a proposal, theory, or system rather than merely agreeing with it privately. A proponent of renewable energy suggests a person who publicly argues for its wider use. It overlaps with advocate, but advocate is also commonly used for someone defending another person’s rights or interests, whereas proponent is particularly closely associated with an idea, plan, theory, or position. A proponent need not have originated the proposal. The word itself does not imply that the supported position is correct.

ja: proponent：提案・理論・政策などを積極的に支持し、その採用を主張する人。
supporter：人・団体・考えなどを支持する人を表す最も一般的な語。
advocate：政策・権利・行動などを公に支持・擁護する人。
champion：人・運動・改革などを熱心かつ力強く推進する人。
backer：計画・事業・候補者などを資金・影響力によって支援する人。
exponent：理論・思想・芸術などを代表し、説明・実践する人物。
opponent：提案・人物・立場などに反対する人。
critic：考え・政策・作品などの欠点を分析し、批判する人。
en: a proponent actively supports and argues for a proposal, theory, policy, or position.
a supporter is the most general term for a person who approves of or assists a person, group, or idea.
an advocate publicly supports or defends a policy, right, action, or another person’s interests.
a champion vigorously promotes a person, movement, reform, or cause.
a backer supports a project, business, or candidate through money, influence, or practical assistance.
an exponent represents, explains, or practices a particular theory, philosophy, or artistic style.
an opponent is a person who opposes a proposal, position, or individual.
a critic analyzes and points out defects in an idea, policy, work, or performance.

etymology.ja: proponent はラテン語 proponens に由来し、これは proponere「前に置く、提示する、提案する」の現在分詞である。proponere は pro-「前に」と ponere「置く」から構成される。したがって proponent は本来、考え・命題・計画などを人々の前に提示する者を意味した。そこから、その提案を提出するだけでなく、その正当性を主張し、採用を推進する人物を表すようになった。propose「提案する」、proposal「提案」、proposition「命題・提案」も同じラテン語系統に属する。
etymology.en: Proponent derives from Latin proponens, the present participle of proponere, meaning to put forward or propose. Proponere is formed from pro-, meaning forward, and ponere, meaning to place. A proponent was therefore originally a person who placed an idea, proposition, or plan before others. The meaning expanded from merely presenting the proposal to defending its merits and promoting its adoption. Propose, proposal, and proposition belong to the same Latin word family.

note.ja: 特定の政策・権利・理念などを公に支持し、その実現を求める人。
note.en: A person who publicly supports a policy, right, or cause and argues for its implementation.

note.ja: 人・組織・計画・考えなどに賛成し、支援する人を広く表す。
note.en: The broad term for someone who approves of or assists a person, organization, plan, or idea.

note.ja: 運動・改革・集団などを熱心かつ公然と擁護・推進する人物。
note.en: A person who enthusiastically and publicly defends or promotes a movement, reform, or group.

note.ja: 特定の理論・思想・方法・芸術様式などを代表し、説明・実践する人。
note.en: A person who represents, explains, or practices a particular theory, philosophy, method, or artistic style.

note.ja: 資金・影響力・実務的支援によって計画・事業・候補者などを支える人。
note.en: A person who supports a project, business, or candidate with money, influence, or practical assistance.

a proponent of free trade — 自由貿易の提唱者

ja: She has long been a proponent of greater investment in public transportation. — 彼女は長年、公共交通機関への投資拡大を提唱してきた。
Proponents of the policy argue that it will reduce regional inequality. — その政策の支持者たちは、政策によって地域格差が縮小すると主張している。
He became a leading proponent of using technology in education. — 彼は教育における技術利用の主要な推進者となった。
Even its strongest proponents acknowledge that the proposal involves significant risks. — その提案の最も強力な支持者たちでさえ、重大なリスクを伴うことを認めている。
Proponents of utility model protection argue that it offers a faster and less expensive means of protecting incremental technical innovation. — 実用新案による保護の支持者は、それが段階的な技術革新を迅速かつ低費用で保護する手段になると主張している。
en: She has long been a proponent of greater investment in public transportation.
Proponents of the policy argue that it will reduce regional inequality.
He became a leading proponent of using technology in education.
Even its strongest proponents acknowledge that the proposal involves significant risks.
Proponents of utility model protection argue that it offers a faster and less expensive means of protecting incremental technical innovation.

patterns: an opponent in + contest / election / debate

usage.opposition: An opponent of a policy or proposal is someone who actively disagrees with or resists it.
usage.competition: In sports, elections, games, and debates, an opponent is the person or team competing against another.
usage.prepositions: Use of for the object opposed and in for the contest: an opponent of the policy; her opponent in the election.
usage.not_enemy: An opponent competes with or opposes someone but is not necessarily an enemy or personally hostile.
usage.legal_context: In legal discussion, opponent can describe the other side informally, but opposing party, adverse party, respondent, or defendant may be more precise.
usage.register: The word is natural in everyday, political, sporting, academic, and professional communication.

ja: 試合・競技・ゲームなどで競い合う相手
選挙・討論・競争などで対立する候補者・人物
政策・提案・制度などに反対する人
議論において反対の立場を主張する人・集団
訴訟・交渉などで反対側に立つ当事者
活動・改革などの実施を阻止しようとする人物
en: a person or team competing against another in a sport, contest, or game
a candidate or person competing against another in an election, debate, or competition
someone who disagrees with and opposes a policy, proposal, or system
a person or group arguing for the contrary position in a discussion
a party taking the opposing side in litigation or negotiation
someone attempting to prevent the introduction of an activity or reform

nuance.ja: opponent は、ある人と直接競争する相手と、特定の考え・政策に反対する人の両方を表す。スポーツでは defeat an opponent「対戦相手を破る」、政治では an opponent of the reform「改革への反対者」のように使う。enemy と異なり、個人的な憎悪や武力的な敵対を意味せず、試合後も相手を尊重できる。competitor は同じ市場・大会などで利益や順位を競うことに重点があり、必ずしも相手の意見に反対しているわけではない。proponent と対比する場合、opponent は特定の提案・立場の採用に反対する側を表す。
nuance.en: Opponent can describe both a direct competitor and a person who opposes a particular idea or policy. In sport, one defeats or faces an opponent; in politics, an opponent of reform argues against the proposed change. Unlike enemy, opponent does not necessarily imply personal hatred, armed hostility, or a desire to cause harm. Competitor emphasizes pursuit of the same prize, market, or ranking and does not necessarily imply disagreement with another person’s position. When contrasted with proponent, opponent means the individual or side arguing against the adoption of a proposal or viewpoint.

ja: opponent：競技・選挙などで争う相手、または提案・政策への反対者。
proponent：提案・理論・政策などを積極的に支持・推進する人。
competitor：同じ市場・賞・順位・目標などをめぐって競う人・企業。
rival：長期間にわたり同じ目標・地位を争う競争相手。
adversary：対立・訴訟・戦いなどで向かい合う敵対的な相手。やや形式的。
enemy：人・国家などに強い敵意を持ち、害を与えようとする敵。
critic：考え・政策・作品などの欠点を指摘し、否定的に評価する人。
opposing party：訴訟・交渉などで反対側に立つ当事者。
en: an opponent is a person or team one competes against or someone opposing a proposal or policy.
a proponent actively supports and promotes a proposal, theory, policy, or position.
a competitor pursues the same market, prize, ranking, or objective as another person or company.
a rival competes over time for the same objective, position, or status.
an adversary is a relatively formal term for a hostile opposing party in conflict, litigation, or struggle.
an enemy is a person or state regarded with hostility and potentially an intention to cause harm.
a critic identifies defects in and expresses a negative judgment about an idea, policy, or work.
an opposing party is the party taking the other side in litigation or negotiation.

etymology.ja: opponent はラテン語 opponens に由来し、これは opponere「～に対して置く、対抗させる」の現在分詞である。opponere は ob-「～に対して」と ponere「置く」から構成され、文字どおりには「向かい側に置く」という意味を持った。そこから、議論で反対の立場を取る人、さらに試合・選挙・競争などで向かい合う相手を表すようになった。oppose「反対する」、opposition「反対・野党・対抗」、opposing「反対側の」も同じ語族に属する。
etymology.en: Opponent derives from Latin opponens, the present participle of opponere, meaning to place against or set in opposition. Opponere combines ob-, meaning against, with ponere, meaning to place. The original idea was therefore placing someone or something on the opposite side. The noun developed from a person taking the contrary side in an argument into a general term for someone faced in sport, elections, competition, or conflict. Oppose, opposition, and opposing belong to the same word family.

note.ja: 市場・大会・試験などで、同じ利益・賞・順位を目指して競争する相手。
note.en: A person or organization competing for the same market, prize, ranking, or advantage.

note.ja: 同じ地位・成功・優位性をめぐって継続的に争う競争相手。
note.en: A person or organization engaged in continuing competition for the same position, success, or superiority.

note.ja: 争い・訴訟・対立において反対側に立つ、やや形式的で敵対性の強い語。
note.en: A relatively formal and more hostile term for the opposing side in conflict, litigation, or struggle.

note.ja: 人・計画・作品などを否定的に評価し、その価値を低く述べる人。
note.en: A person who criticizes and attempts to reduce the perceived value of someone, a plan, or a work.

note.ja: 計画・手続き・提案などに対して、正式または明示的に異議を述べる人。
note.en: A person who formally or expressly raises an objection to a plan, procedure, or proposal.

ja: She defeated a much more experienced opponent in the final. — 彼女は決勝で、はるかに経験豊富な対戦相手を破った。
He treated his political opponents with respect despite their sharp disagreements. — 彼は激しい意見の相違にもかかわらず、政治上の対立者に敬意をもって接した。
Opponents of the development plan argue that it will damage the local environment. — その開発計画への反対者は、計画が地域環境を損なうと主張している。
Never underestimate an opponent merely because they appear inexperienced. — 経験が浅そうに見えるというだけで、相手を決して過小評価してはいけない。
The opponent in the patent dispute challenged both the validity of the patent and the allegation of infringement. — 特許紛争の相手方は、特許の有効性と侵害の主張の双方を争った。
en: She defeated a much more experienced opponent in the final.
He treated his political opponents with respect despite their sharp disagreements.
Opponents of the development plan argue that it will damage the local environment.
Never underestimate an opponent merely because they appear inexperienced.
The opponent in the patent dispute challenged both the validity of the patent and the allegation of infringement.

grammar.transitivity: transitive or intransitive depending on construction

usage.person_object: When a person receives payment or another benefit, that person is the direct object: compensate the customer.
usage.reason: Use for to identify the loss, injury, inconvenience, or service for which compensation is provided.
usage.offset: Compensate for means counterbalancing a disadvantage, weakness, loss, or deficiency.
usage.means: With can introduce the payment or benefit provided: compensate employees with additional leave.
usage.passive: Be compensated for is common when focusing on the recipient: Customers were compensated for the delay.
usage.legal_scope: The availability and amount of legal compensation depend on the applicable law, contract, causation, and type of loss.

ja: 損失・損害・負担などについて、人に金銭その他の利益を与えて補償する
労働・役務・貢献などに対して報酬を支払う
欠点・不足・不利益などを別の利点によって埋め合わせる
失われた量・価値・効果と釣り合うよう調整する
身体・機械・制度などが機能の低下を別の働きによって補う
en: to provide a person with money or another benefit for loss, damage, or inconvenience
to pay or reward someone for work, services, or contribution
to counterbalance a weakness, deficiency, or disadvantage with another benefit
to make an adjustment corresponding to a lost amount, value, or effect
for a body, machine, or system, to offset reduced function through another process

nuance.ja: compensate には、人に補償・報酬を与える意味と、不足・不利益を相殺する意味がある。The airline compensated the passengers for the delay では passengers が補償を受ける人、delay が補償の理由である。一方、The lower price compensates for the limited features では、低価格が機能の少なさを埋め合わせる。compensate は必ずしも損失を完全に消滅させることを意味せず、部分的に釣り合わせる場合にも使える。法律上の「補償」「損害賠償」は法域や請求原因により compensation、damages、restitution などの区別があるため、日本語から機械的に compensate と訳せるとは限らない。
nuance.en: Compensate has two principal uses: providing compensation or remuneration to a person, and offsetting a deficiency or disadvantage. In The airline compensated the passengers for the delay, passengers identifies the recipients and delay identifies the reason. In The lower price compensates for the limited features, one advantage counterbalances a disadvantage. The verb does not necessarily mean eliminating the loss completely; partial counterbalancing may be sufficient. In law, concepts translated generally as compensation or damages differ by jurisdiction and cause of action, so compensate, pay damages, and provide restitution are not automatically interchangeable.

ja: compensate：損失について人に補償する、または欠点・不足を埋め合わせる。
compensate for：不利益・不足・弱点などを相殺・補完する。
reimburse：人が実際に支払った費用を払い戻す。
indemnify：契約・法律に基づき、特定の損失・責任から人を補償・保護する。
pay damages：不法行為・契約違反などによる損害について賠償金を支払う。
remunerate：労働・役務について金銭的報酬を与える。形式的。
offset：一方の損失・費用・影響を、別の利益・量によって相殺する。
make up for：損失・失敗・不足を埋め合わせる日常的な表現。
en: compensate means providing payment for a loss or counterbalancing a weakness or deficiency.
compensate for means offsetting or making up for a disadvantage, shortage, or weakness.
reimburse means repaying money that a person has actually spent.
indemnify means compensating or protecting someone against specified loss or liability under law or contract.
pay damages means paying a monetary remedy for loss caused by a legal wrong such as infringement or breach.
remunerate formally means paying someone for work or services.
offset means balancing one loss, cost, or effect against another benefit or quantity.
make up for is an everyday expression for compensating for a loss, failure, or deficiency.

etymology.ja: compensate はラテン語 compensare「釣り合わせる、相殺する」に由来する。これは com-「ともに、相互に」と pensare「重さを量る、評価する」から構成され、pensare は pendere「つるす、量る」と関係する。原義は、天秤の一方に生じた不足を他方の重さで釣り合わせることであった。そこから、不利益を別の利益で埋め合わせる意味と、損失・労働などに対応する金銭を与える意味が発達した。compensation、compensatory、recompense なども、価値を量り釣り合わせるという発想を共有する。
etymology.en: Compensate derives from Latin compensare, meaning to balance or counterbalance. It combines com-, meaning together or mutually, with pensare, meaning to weigh or evaluate, which is related to pendere, to hang or weigh. The original image was balancing a deficiency on one side of a scale with weight on the other. From this developed both the sense of counterbalancing a disadvantage with another benefit and the sense of providing payment corresponding to a loss or service. Compensation, compensatory, and recompense share the underlying idea of weighing and restoring balance.

note.ja: 交通費・購入費・医療費など、人が実際に支出した金額を払い戻す。
note.en: To repay an amount that someone actually spent on travel, purchases, medical care, or another expense.

note.ja: 契約・法律上の仕組みにより、人を特定の損失・責任から補償または保護する。
note.en: To compensate or protect a person against specified loss or liability through a legal or contractual arrangement.

note.ja: 仕事・役務・専門的貢献に対して人へ報酬を支払う形式的な語。
note.en: A formal verb meaning to pay someone for work, services, or professional contribution.

note.ja: 費用・損失・排出量などを、反対方向の利益・削減・数量によって相殺する。
note.en: To counterbalance a cost, loss, emission, or other effect with an opposing benefit, reduction, or quantity.

note.ja: 不足・失敗・遅延などによる不利益を、別の行動や利点によって埋め合わせる。
note.en: To counterbalance a shortage, failure, delay, or disadvantage through another action or benefit.

compensate someone for damage — 損害について人を補償する
compensate customers for a delay — 遅延について顧客を補償する
compensate employees fairly — 従業員へ公正に報酬を与える
be fully compensated — 全額・十分に補償される
be adequately compensated — 適切に補償される
compensate for a weakness — 弱点を補う
compensate for a lack of experience — 経験不足を補う

be fully compensated

ja: The airline compensated the passengers for the lengthy delay. — 航空会社は長時間の遅延について乗客を補償した。
Employees should be fairly compensated for working additional hours. — 従業員は追加の時間働いたことについて、公正に報酬を受けるべきだ。
The excellent location more than compensates for the apartment’s small size. — 素晴らしい立地は、そのアパートの狭さを補って余りある。
The system automatically adjusts the signal to compensate for changes in temperature. — そのシステムは温度変化を補正するため、自動的に信号を調整する。

A patent owner may seek monetary relief to compensate for loss caused by infringement, although the available remedy depends on the applicable law. — 特許権者は侵害によって生じた損失を補償するため金銭的救済を求め得るが、利用可能な救済は適用法によって異なる。

Employees should be fairly compensated for working additional hours.
The excellent location more than compensates for the apartment’s small size.
The system automatically adjusts the signal to compensate for changes in temperature.
A patent owner may seek monetary relief to compensate for loss caused by infringement, although the available remedy depends on the applicable law.

usage.physical: For a person, clumsy commonly means moving without sufficient coordination and frequently dropping, hitting, or damaging things.
usage.object: For an object or design, it means awkward, inconvenient, heavy, or difficult to use.
usage.method: For an attempt or solution, it means poorly executed, inefficient, or lacking refinement.
usage.communication: For words or social behavior, it means tactless, insensitive, or awkwardly expressed.
usage.prepositions: Clumsy with commonly introduces an object; clumsy at introduces an activity or skill.
usage.comparison: The final y changes to i before -er and -est: clumsier and clumsiest.

ja: 身体の動きがぎこちなく、物を落としたりぶつけたりしやすい
手先の扱いが不器用で、細かな作業が不得意な
道具・装置・設計などが扱いにくく、洗練されていない
方法・試み・文章などが不自然で、うまく構成されていない
発言・対応などが不器用で、相手への配慮や機転を欠く
en: moving awkwardly and tending to drop, strike, or damage things
lacking skill or coordination in handling objects or performing delicate tasks
for a tool, device, or design, awkward, inconvenient, or lacking refinement
for a method, attempt, or sentence, poorly constructed or inelegantly executed
for speech or behavior, awkward, tactless, or insufficiently sensitive

nuance.ja: clumsy は、身体的な不器用さから、設計・文章・人間関係上の不手際まで広く使われる。He’s clumsy は、よく物を落としたり家具にぶつかったりする人物を示しやすい。a clumsy device は、機能しないとは限らないが、大きすぎる、重い、操作しにくいなど、使い勝手が悪いことを表す。a clumsy apology は、謝罪する意思はあっても表現が不自然または配慮不足であることを示す。awkward と重なるが、clumsy は技能・設計・実行の不十分さを強く示し、awkward は気まずい社会状況や不便な姿勢・配置にもさらに広く使える。人に直接 clumsy と言うと批判的に響く。
nuance.en: Clumsy applies broadly from physical lack of coordination to defects in design, language, and social conduct. He’s clumsy commonly describes someone who drops objects or bumps into furniture. A clumsy device may function but remain excessively large, heavy, inconvenient, or difficult to operate. A clumsy apology may be sincere in intention but awkwardly expressed or insufficiently considerate. Clumsy overlaps with awkward, but clumsy more strongly suggests inadequate skill, design, or execution, whereas awkward extends more readily to embarrassing social situations and inconvenient positions or arrangements. Directly calling a person clumsy can sound critical.

ja: clumsy：動作・扱い・表現・設計などが不器用で、ぎこちない。
awkward：動作・状況・表現などが不自然、不便、または気まずい。
uncoordinated：身体各部の動きがうまく連携していない。
inept：技能・判断が著しく不足し、仕事や対応が不適切な。
bungling：不注意・無能さによって繰り返し失敗する。
cumbersome：物・制度・手続きなどが大きい、複雑、または扱いにくい。
tactless：相手の感情・状況への配慮を欠く発言・行動をする。
graceful：動き・形・表現などが滑らかで、優雅な。
en: clumsy describes movement, handling, expression, or design that is awkward and lacking skill.
awkward describes movement, situations, or expressions that are uncomfortable, inconvenient, or socially embarrassing.
uncoordinated means lacking effective cooperation among the movements of different parts of the body.
inept suggests a serious lack of skill or judgment resulting in ineffective conduct.
bungling describes repeated mistakes caused by incompetence or carelessness.
cumbersome describes an object, system, or procedure that is large, complicated, or difficult to handle.
tactless describes speech or behavior lacking sensitivity to another person’s feelings or circumstances.
graceful describes movement, form, or expression that is smooth, controlled, and elegant.

etymology.ja: clumsy は、現在では廃れた英語の動詞 clumse「しびれさせる、しびれる」に由来するとされる。この語はおそらくスカンディナヴィア系で、スウェーデン語方言の klumsig「しびれた、不器用な」などと関係する。もとは寒さなどで身体がしびれ、思うように動けない状態を表し、そこから動作がぎこちない、不器用であるという意味が発達した。さらに、手で扱いにくい物、洗練されていない方法、不自然な文章、配慮を欠く対応などにも比喩的に使われるようになった。
etymology.en: Clumsy is generally derived from the obsolete English verb clumse, meaning to make or become numb. The word was probably of Scandinavian origin and is associated with forms such as dialectal Swedish klumsig, meaning numb or clumsy. It originally suggested moving as though one’s body were numb from cold and therefore difficult to control. From physical awkwardness, the adjective expanded to objects difficult to handle, poorly refined methods, inelegant language, and socially insensitive behavior.

note.ja: 動作・姿勢・道具・会話・社会的状況などが不自然または気まずい。
note.en: Describes movement, posture, tools, conversation, or social situations that are uncomfortable or unnatural.

note.ja: 身体の各部分を滑らかに連動させることが難しい。
note.en: Describes difficulty making different parts of the body move together smoothly.

note.ja: 技能・判断力が不十分で、仕事・対応などを効果的に行えない。
note.en: Suggests insufficient skill or judgment resulting in ineffective work or conduct.

note.ja: 装置・制度・文章などが大きい、重い、複雑などの理由で扱いにくい。
note.en: Describes equipment, systems, or language that is difficult to use because of size, weight, or complexity.

note.ja: 発言・行動が相手の気持ちに配慮せず、傷つけたり不快にさせたりする。
note.en: Describes speech or behavior that fails to consider another person’s feelings and may cause offense.

His clumsy movements knocked several books off the shelf.

usage.position: Approximately normally appears immediately before the number, quantity, measurement, or expression it modifies.
usage.precision: It indicates that the stated value is close to the actual value but is not exact.
usage.direction: Unlike nearly, approximately does not normally indicate whether the true value is above or below the stated figure.
usage.register: It is more formal and technical than about, around, or roughly.
usage.abbreviation: Approx. is used in notes, tables, labels, and informal technical material but may be avoided in continuous formal prose.
usage.symbol: The symbol ≈ means approximately equal to and is used chiefly in mathematical and scientific notation.

ja: 数値・数量などが正確ではないが、その値に近く
時刻・期間・距離などについて、およそ・約
測定値・計算結果などが一定の誤差を含みながら近似的に
二つの量・形・状態などが完全ではないものの、ほぼ等しく
入手可能な情報に基づく概算・推定として
en: for a number or quantity, close to but not exactly the stated value
for a time, duration, or distance, roughly or about
for a measurement or calculation, as an approximation allowing some error
for two quantities, forms, or conditions, nearly but not perfectly equally
as an estimate based on the information currently available

nuance.ja: approximately は、数値が厳密ではないことを明示しつつ、合理的に近い値を示す。approximately 100 people なら、実際の人数が100人より少ない場合にも多い場合にも使える。これに対して nearly 100 people は通常「100人には届かないが、それに近い人数」を表す。roughly は概算の幅が比較的大きい印象を与えることがあり、about と around は日常会話でより自然である。契約・特許・技術仕様では approximately が許容範囲を自動的に確定するわけではないため、数値の境界が重要なら、公差・測定方法・具体的範囲を明記する必要がある。
nuance.en: Approximately signals that a figure is not exact but is reasonably close to the stated value. Approximately 100 people can describe an actual number either below or above 100. By contrast, nearly 100 people normally means a number below but close to 100. Roughly may suggest a broader or less carefully calculated estimate, while about and around are more conversational. In contracts, patent claims, and technical specifications, approximately does not automatically establish a precise tolerance. When numerical boundaries matter, the permitted range, measurement method, or tolerance should be expressly defined.

ja: approximately：正確ではないが合理的に近い値で、約・およそ。
about：数量・時刻などについて「約」を表す最も一般的な語。
around：about と同様に、数値・時刻などがおよそであることを表す口語的な語。
roughly：細かな正確さを求めない大まかな概算として。
nearly：一定の値には達していないが、非常に近く。
almost：状態・数量が完全な段階には達していないが、あとわずかで。
more or less：多少の差を許容して、おおむね・だいたい。
exactly：誤差や概算を含まず、正確に。
en: approximately means close to but not exactly a stated number, measurement, or value.
about is the most general word for indicating an inexact quantity or time.
around is a conversational alternative to about for an estimated number or time.
roughly presents a value as a broad estimate without fine precision.
nearly normally means below but very close to a particular number or state.
almost means close to but not fully reaching a particular state or quantity.
more or less means generally or approximately while allowing some variation.
exactly means with complete precision and without approximation or error.

etymology.ja: approximately は形容詞・動詞 approximate に副詞接尾辞 -ly を加えた語である。approximate はラテン語 approximare「近づける、近づく」に由来し、ad-「～へ」と proximus「最も近い」から構成される。proximus は near を意味する prope と関係する。したがって approximately の根本的な発想は、完全に一致するのではなく、ある値・状態へ近づいていることである。同じ語族には approximation「近似・概算」と proximity「近接」がある。
etymology.en: Approximately is formed from approximate with the adverbial suffix -ly. Approximate derives from Latin approximare, meaning to bring near or come near, and combines ad-, meaning toward, with proximus, meaning nearest. Proximus is related to prope, meaning near. The underlying idea of approximately is therefore approaching a value or condition without coinciding with it exactly. Related words include approximation, meaning an estimated or near value, and proximity, meaning nearness.

note.ja: 数値・時刻・距離などが正確ではなく、おおよその値であることを表す一般語。
note.en: The general word for indicating that a number, time, or distance is not exact.

note.ja: 細部の精度を重視しない、大まかな計算・推定であることを強調する。
note.en: Emphasizes that a figure is a broad calculation or estimate without fine precision.

note.ja: 数値・時刻などについて、about と同様に「およそ」を表す口語的な語。
note.en: A conversational word meaning about when used with a number, quantity, or time.

note.ja: 多少の違いや例外はあるものの、全体としておおむね当てはまる。
note.en: Means generally or approximately, while allowing some difference or exceptions.

note.ja: 主として年代・日付の前で「およそ」を表す形式的な語で、c. と略される。
note.en: A formal term used mainly before an approximate year or date and often abbreviated as c.

usage.outcome: Ultimately can identify the final result reached after a process, series of events, or period of uncertainty.
usage.fundamental: It can also mean at the most basic or decisive level: The decision is ultimately yours.
usage.position: It can appear initially, medially, or before the principal verb, depending on emphasis.
usage.not_sequence: It does not normally mean last in a simple list of actions; finally or lastly may be more appropriate there.
usage.responsibility: Ultimately responsible emphasizes the person or institution bearing final or fundamental responsibility.
usage.register: The word is natural in conversation but especially common in analytical, professional, academic, and legal writing.

ja: 一連の出来事・検討・変化を経た最終的な結果として
長い時間や複数の試みの末に、結局は
多数の要因を突き詰めた最も根本的な水準では
最終的な決定権・責任・支配がある場所または人物において
表面的な事情ではなく、決定的な原因・目的に関して言えば
en: as the final result of a process, discussion, or series of events
eventually, after a long period or several attempts
at the most fundamental level after all relevant factors are considered
with reference to the person or institution holding final authority or responsibility
in relation to the decisive cause or purpose rather than superficial circumstances

nuance.ja: ultimately は、時間的な最終結果と、論理的・根本的な帰着の双方を表す。The negotiations ultimately failed では、交渉の過程を経た末に失敗したという時間的結果である。The decision is ultimately yours では、最後に決めるという時間順序よりも、最終的な決定権があなたにあることを示す。eventually は時間の経過後に何かが起きることを強調し、finally は待機・困難・順序の末の最後を表しやすい。ultimately は複数の事情を考慮した上での最終的・決定的な帰結を示すため、分析・議論・法律文書で特に有用である。
nuance.en: Ultimately expresses both a final result in time and a fundamental or logical conclusion. The negotiations ultimately failed describes the outcome reached after the negotiation process. The decision is ultimately yours concerns final authority rather than merely the chronological order of making the decision. Eventually emphasizes that something happens after the passage of time, while finally often emphasizes the end of a wait, difficulty, or sequence. Ultimately is particularly useful in analytical, argumentative, and legal contexts because it identifies the decisive conclusion remaining after multiple considerations have been taken into account.

ja: ultimately：一連の過程の最終結果として、または突き詰めれば根本的に。
eventually：時間が経過した後、最終的にある出来事が起こって。
finally：待機・困難・順序などの末に、ついに・最後に。
in the end：さまざまな出来事・検討の後で、結局。
at last：長く待ったり努力したりした末に、ついに。感情を伴いやすい。
fundamentally：問題の最も基本的・本質的な水準で。
basically：細部を除き、基本的には。会話でもよく使う。
decisively：疑問・争いを終わらせるほど決定的な方法で。
en: ultimately means as the final outcome or, at the deepest level, when all considerations are reduced to what is decisive.
eventually means after a period of time, often without specifying exactly when.
finally emphasizes the end of a wait, difficulty, process, or sequence.
in the end means after all events, discussions, or considerations have occurred.
at last means after a long wait or effort and often conveys relief or another emotion.
fundamentally means at the most basic or essential level of a matter.
basically means in the most important respects while excluding unnecessary detail.
decisively means in a manner sufficient to settle a question, contest, or dispute.

etymology.ja: ultimately は形容詞 ultimate に副詞接尾辞 -ly を加えた語である。ultimate はラテン語 ultimus「最も遠い、最後の、最終の」に由来し、比較を表す語 ultra「～を越えて、さらに先に」と関係する。空間的に最も遠い地点という考えから、時間的な最後、過程の最終結果、さらに論理的に突き詰めた根本的な原因・原理という意味が発達した。ultimate は日常語で「最高の」という意味を持つこともあるが、ultimately は通常「最終的に」または「根本的には」を表す。
etymology.en: Ultimately is formed from the adjective ultimate with the adverbial suffix -ly. Ultimate derives from Latin ultimus, meaning farthest, last, or final, and is related to ultra, meaning beyond. The spatial idea of the farthest point developed into the final point in time, the eventual outcome of a process, and the fundamental cause or principle reached when an analysis is carried to its limit. Although ultimate can informally mean the greatest or best, ultimately normally means in the final result or at the most fundamental level.

note.ja: すぐではないが、時間の経過や複数の出来事の後で最終的に起こる。
note.en: Describes something occurring after time has passed or after several intervening events.

note.ja: 長い待機・努力・困難・一連の段階の終わりに、ついに起こる。
note.en: Describes something occurring at the end of a long wait, effort, difficulty, or sequence.

note.ja: さまざまな出来事・議論・選択を経た結果として「結局」と述べる。
note.en: Introduces the result remaining after various events, discussions, or choices.

note.ja: 表面的な事情ではなく、問題の最も基本的・本質的な水準において。
note.en: At the most basic or essential level of a matter rather than in its superficial details.

note.ja: 複雑な外見を取り除いて考えれば、根本的にはという形式的な表現。
note.en: A formal expression meaning fundamentally, once the complexity or surface appearance is removed.
